answer: A market can require every agent to post a small bond that stays locked while it trades. A new identity starts with a narrow trellis of allowed partners and earns wider access only after repeated honest trades build a public signal of reliability. Creating hundreds of fake agents then stops paying: each clone needs its own bond, and the delta between a fresh identity and a trusted one is real trading history that cannot be copied in a day. An attacker would have to fund and age every clone, which makes a sybil swarm expensive and slow to weaponize.
